Job 01

I have transcripts from a discovery call

Turning raw notes, recordings and client documents into structured evidence you can build on. This is the front door of almost every engagement.

Run thisWhat it doesNeedsYou get
/scan-engagementReads a folder of client material and classifies what's in it — what's extractable, what's noise, what's missingA folder with files in itA classified inventory, plus a list of gaps
/chunk-documentSplits a document too large for one pass into workable piecesA PDF, CSV or text fileOrdered chunks, ready to process
Just ask — “interpret these transcripts”
discovery-transcript-interpreter		Extracts pain points, metrics, constraints and stakeholder priorities, each tagged with an evidence IDTranscripts in the engagement's inputs/Evidence, pain-point and metric registers — the inputs every downstream step reads

Put client files in inputs/ rather than pasting them. That's where the scrubber sits. A transcript pasted into the chat goes through exactly as typed.

Job 02

I need a full assessment

The complete Ignite Assess run: discovery, five parallel analyses, roadmap, assembly, dashboard, Excel. Hours, not minutes — and real cost. Reach for it when the engagement genuinely warrants the whole thing.

Run thisWhat it doesNeedsYou get
/run-pipelineRuns the whole assessment end to end, stopping at consultant checkpoints along the wayAn engagement folder with transcripts in inputs/The full deliverable set — assessment, ROI model, roadmap, dashboard, Excel
/generate-assessment-htmlBuilds the assessment dashboard on its own — sidebar navigation, capability heatmaps, ROI scenario toggles, phone-frame prototypesAssessment outputs already producedOne self-contained HTML file, 250–400 KB
Just ask — “run the assessment for…”
value-consulting-orchestrator		Works out which engagement type you're describing and routes to the right pipeline — Assess, Inspire, or bothA sentence describing the engagementRouting, then whichever pipeline fits

You usually don't want the whole pipeline. That's the point of the split. If what you need is the ROI model, or the capability assessment, or the journey maps, go to that section and run just that. The full run is for producing the complete assessment deliverable.

Never hand-build an assessment dashboard. Converting markdown to HTML or writing custom CSS produces something that looks broadly right and is missing the entire design system. If the file is much under 250 KB, it was built the wrong way.

Job 03

I need an ROI model

The most-repeated deliverable in the team, and the one that most rewards running the method rather than reaching for a spreadsheet. Two phases: work out what to model, then work out how much.

Run thisWhat it doesNeedsYou get
/build-roiThe standalone ROI run — identifies the value levers, then quantifies them, without the full assessment around itBank, country, line of business, and the problem being solved. Nothing else.roi_config.json and a written ROI report
/profile-bankPulls a bank's public financials — annual reports, investor decks — and turns them into model inputsA bank name and countryStructured metrics that drop straight into the ROI config, at high confidence instead of estimated
/generate-roi-questionnaireBuilds the client data request, pre-filled with everything Cortex already knows. Turns "fill all this in" into "check what we've got"Whatever upstream work exists — more is better, none still worksA colour-coded Excel questionnaire: green to verify, yellow to fill
/generate-roi-excelProduces the full Excel model — dashboard, cashflows, three scenarios, servicing analysis, assumptionsAn ROI configThe client-ready workbook
Just ask — “what are the levers here?”
roi-hypothesis-builder		Decomposes the problem and derives the value levers, each validated against the four-link chain from root driver to financial impactEvidence, or just a problem statementValidated lever candidates for you to approve
Just ask — “model these levers”
roi-financial-modeler		Turns approved levers into three-scenario projections with the Backbase impact computed from the gapApproved leversThe financial model behind the workbook

The order that works. /profile-bank first so the baseline is real rather than assumed, then /build-roi, then /generate-roi-excel. Use /generate-roi-questionnaire when you need the client to supply numbers you can't get from public sources — it goes out far better pre-filled.

Job 04

I need a deck or a document

Anything client-facing and visual. Start at the router — it asks which format you want and sends you to the right builder, which is more reliable than guessing between four similar names.

Run thisWhat it doesNeedsYou get
/frontlineAsks what you're making, explains the options, routes you. Always start here.NothingThe right builder, already running
/frontline-slides-htmlA deck as a single HTML file — 17 layouts, presenter mode, overview gridYour content and argumentOne .html deck you can iterate on fast
/frontline-slides-pptxThe same deck as a real PowerPoint file that imports cleanly into Google SlidesYour content, ideally settledA shareable .pptx
/frontline-long-formA scrolling document with sidebar navigation — value cases, ROI summaries, executive briefingsYour contentA single HTML document that also prints to PDF

The workflow that saves rework. Draft in /frontline-slides-html while the argument is still moving — it's fast to regenerate. Only convert to /frontline-slides-pptx once the story is settled. This page was built with /frontline-long-form.

Three rules that carry most of the quality. Maximum four points on a slide. Headers say the outcome, not the topic — "Unifying 60% of the bank's manual work", not "Our Platform". Open on From→To.

Job 05

I'm prepping an Ignite workshop

Ignite Inspire is workshop-driven rather than evidence-driven, so it doesn't run through the assessment pipeline at all. Four workshops, each prepared and then run, then synthesised into the Ignite Day deck.

Run thisWhat it doesNeedsYou get
Just ask — “prepare the strategy workshop for…”
workshop-preparation		Researches the client and builds a pre-populated facilitation deck with hypotheses for the room to validate. Four modes: strategy, member, employee, architectureClient documents — annual report, strategy material — and which workshopA checkpoint file for you to approve, then the workshop deck
Just ask — “synthesise the workshops”
ignite-workshop-synthesizer		Reads all four workshop outputs, works out which hypotheses held, and ranks use-case candidatesAll four workshops doneHypothesis validation matrix and prioritised use cases for Ignite Day

Workshop prep runs in two phases on purpose. It writes a checkpoint file and stops, so you can correct the hypotheses before a deck gets built around them. Approving quickly to save time here usually costs more time later.

Ignite Inspire has its own manual. A self-contained subsystem under knowledge/Ignite Inspire/ with eight agent prompts, deck templates, worked example decks, brand assets and a consultant guide. If you're running an Inspire engagement, read its own CLAUDE.md first.

Job 06

I need use cases, journeys or a prototype

The middle layer of an engagement — where a validated opportunity becomes something specific enough to cost, sequence and show.

Run thisWhat it doesNeedsYou get
/build-journeyMaps a customer-to-employee journey with the value leaking at each step quantified, friction called out, and the Backbase-enabled future state beside itDiscovery outputs. Name the journeys or let it recommend by evidence densityJourney maps as JSON and markdown, feeding the dashboard
/usecase-docWrites the full ten-section use case specificationA use case worth specifyingA structured document an implementation team can read
/prototypeBuilds a clickable HTML mockup following the happy path of a use caseA defined use caseA single-file interactive prototype
Just ask — “is this OOTB or custom?”
capability-gap-analyzer		Checks every capability your use cases need against the Backbase product directory and the live InfobankUse cases with their required capabilitiesA matrix splitting out-of-the-box from configuration from custom build
Just ask — “design these use cases”
usecase-designer		Designs use cases that are architecturally grounded, linked to value themes and validated against what the platform actually doesPrioritised opportunities, usually from workshopsDesigned use cases with the gap analysis attached

Run the gap analysis before you commit to a roadmap, not after. It's the difference between a sequence built on what the platform does and one built on what we assumed it does.

Job 07

I need a commercial proposalNew

The newest part of Cortex, and the one with the sharpest internal/client divide. The strategy work and the client document are deliberately separate skills, because they must never leak into each other.

Run thisWhat it doesNeedsYou get
/proposal-builderNot yet mergedThe deal cockpit. Reads what the engagement already knows, interviews you only on the genuine gaps, then works the strategy — story model, anchor, lever families, Good/Better/Best, the concession ladder, approval tiers, the Deal Desk gateA deal entering the pricing conversation. Pricing supplied fresh each run — never storedThe internal strategy pack and the client proposal, with a hard wall between them
/proposal-longformNot yet mergedThe client-facing document on its own — branded, sidebar-navigated, with a language toggle including right-to-left Arabic, live pricing sliders, and a one-click executive readout PDFContent you've already settledOne self-contained HTML proposal the client can open anywhere
/deal-notesNot yet mergedFeeds what happened in the last client meeting back into the deal, and reports what changed against the planA transcript or your bullets from the meetingUpdated deal state and a delta report — what moved, which levers just became available, what to do next round
/pricing-modelNot yet mergedThe deterministic pricing engine underneath the other threePricing inputsComputed pricing every render reconciles to
/upgrade-analysisWorks out a client's packaging migration path and builds the case for the tier moveAccount context — current products, packaging, ARRThe outside-in point of view, tier value articulation and upgrade business case

Anything prefixed INTERNAL_ never goes to a client. Negotiation plans, deal state, delta reports, Deal Desk fields. The rendering skill is built so it cannot read those files, and /publish excludes them — but the prefix is also there so you can see at a glance what must not be attached to an email.

Every number comes from the engine, not from the model reasoning about it. One config, one engine, all renders reconciled to the penny. If a figure in a proposal disagrees with the model, that's a bug worth reporting rather than something to correct by hand.

Job 08

What do we already know about this?

Cortex accumulates every engagement. These are the ways to ask it what it has — before you research something the team already did.

Run thisWhat it doesNeedsYou get
/domain-contextThe overall picture for a line of business — start here if you're new to the domainA domain: retail, commercial, sme, wealth, investing or corporateOrientation on how that line of business works
/domain-benchmarksBenchmarks and KPIs to anchor an assessment or an ROI caseA domain, optionally a journeySourced reference figures
/domain-pain-pointsThe problems that show up repeatedly in this domainA domainRecurring pain points with the evidence behind them
/domain-journeysReference journey mapsA domainJourneys you can start from rather than invent
/domain-usecasesUse cases that have worked elsewhereA domainProven use cases with context
/domain-value-propsThe value propositions that land with this audienceA domainPositioning that has already been tested
Just ask — “find me a defensible benchmark for…”
benchmark-librarian		Curates benchmarks with a source and a confidence rating on each, and excludes anything from a test engagementWhat you need a reference point forBenchmarks you can put in front of a CFO

Anything tagged [Synthetic-Test] is fictional and must never reach a client deliverable. Test engagements were once harvested into shared knowledge as if they were real, and a fabricated call-volume benchmark made it into a live client workbook before it was caught. Retrieval now excludes them — but if you ever see that tag in an output, stop and report it.

Job 09

I'm done — pressure-test it, share it, bank the learning

The last mile. One of these makes the work better before it goes out; the rest make sure the next engagement starts further ahead than this one did.

Run thisWhat it doesNeedsYou get
/crittyNot yet mergedTurns the critical dial to maximum and attacks the current work — assumptions, weak evidence, unearned conclusionsSomething worth challenging. Run it before anything important goes outA hard critique. It's meant to sting.
/publishCommits, pushes and opens a pull request. You never touch gitWork that's ready for reviewA PR, and your changes safely off your laptop
/reconcileChecks every open PR for conflicts, merges the clean ones, resolves the restPRs piling upA tidy repository
/extract-learningsPulls the reusable knowledge out of a finished engagement and files it, anonymisedA closed engagementKnowledge entries the whole team retrieves later
/log-modificationRecords that you had to fix an agent's output by hand, and whyAny time you rewrite something Cortex producedThe signal that decides what gets improved next

/log-modification is thirty seconds that compounds. Nobody watches you edit an output. If you fix the same weakness on every engagement and never log it, it stays broken for everyone, forever. It's the cheapest contribution anyone on the team can make.

Publishing is blocked if there's no knowledge harvest. Deliberately. An engagement that produces outputs but no learnings leaves the system exactly as clever as it was before.

Under the hood

The agents the pipeline runs for you. You can now invoke any of them on their own — that's what the split changed — but in most cases the command above is the better door, because it sets up the inputs correctly first.

AgentRuns atWhat it produces
discovery-transcript-interpreterDiscoveryEvidence, pain-point and metric registers — everything downstream reads these
capability-assessmentAnalysisCurrent-state maturity scored against evidence, with the gaps and what they cost
market-context-researcherAnalysisOutside-in context — annual report metrics, peer comparison, public CX data
roi-hypothesis-builderAnalysisThe value levers worth modelling
roi-financial-modelerAnalysisThree-scenario financial projections
journey-builderAnalysisJourney maps with value leakage quantified per step
benchmark-librarianSupportingSourced, confidence-rated benchmarks for anything that needs a reference point
roadmap-prioritizationSequencingA phased roadmap with dependencies, decision gates and value milestones
narrative-assemblerAssemblyEverything above, packaged into one deliverable that reads as a single argument
knowledge-harvesterAutomaticAnonymised learnings, filed after every run. Don't invoke this by hand.
roi-business-case-builderDeprecated—Replaced by roi-hypothesis-builder and roi-financial-modeler. Use those.

What the split changed. Each of these agents used to keep its operating instructions inside the orchestrator script, which is why running one on its own wasn't possible. The instructions now live in the agent itself. The pipeline runs exactly as it did — but every step in it also stands alone.

Reference

Core team only

Here for completeness. If you use Cortex to do consulting work rather than to build Cortex, none of this affects you.

Changing Cortex itself

Any change to an agent, a skill, a template or pipeline code goes through the lifecycle — /bb-prd, /bb-design, /bb-tickets, /bb-build, /bb-pr-review, /bb-refine — with the eval suite as the gate that decides whether it can merge. A hook blocks direct edits to those paths, so this isn't something you can forget to do.

Adding a skill or an agent also means adding it to docs/rollout/catalog.yaml and regenerating this page, in the same PR. CI enforces both — catalog-drift.yml fails a PR whose catalog disagrees with the repo, or whose generated page is behind the catalog. Run python3 tools/build_cheatsheet.py before pushing.

Telemetry

/sync-telemetry pushes journal telemetry up as a GitHub issue, and /process-meeting runs the Cortex standup. Telemetry is intake only — it feeds the backlog that decides what gets built next. Nothing auto-implements; the autonomous development loop was removed in June 2026 because it changed agents outside the gate.

Contributing knowledge is open to everyone. The restriction is on architecture, not content. Anyone can add to knowledge/learnings/, knowledge/domains/ and benchmarks/ — and that's the contribution that makes the biggest difference to everyone else's next engagement.

If something here is wrong, that's the most useful thing you can tell us

A command that doesn't exist, an output that doesn't match the description, a step that fails on your machine — it means this page has drifted from the system. Say so in the team channel, or run /log-modification if you had to fix an output by hand.
